Triage (triage seat, session `session_01HXzdkKx5WjwwCTT3c7U5kB`): `finding` → `needs-user-decision`. Declared-but-unenforced key (`defaultChildren`: 4 declaration sites, 11 producers, 0 consumers — designer drag-drop reads only `defaultProps`), AND it is published to plugin authors in `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md`. Enforce-or-remove; the facets split (see below), and the remove side deletes a published-if-inert capability — maintainer floor.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- platform long-term coherence: both routes close a declared≠enforced gap; A (wire the read) makes the published plugin-author contract true, B (retire the key) shrinks the surface. Leaving it as-is is the only wrong option.
- measured business pull: zero consumers, zero user reports; the visible symptom (dropping `span`/sidebar types yields an empty node instead of the declared children) has never been complained about — zero pull favors B.
- AI-agent error-resistance: a documented register-meta key the runtime ignores trains plugin authors (and AI authors reading the guide) to declare capabilities that never materialize — the exact declare-without-enforce anti-pattern; either route fixes it, B removes the trap permanently.
- startup scope discipline: A is a one-line wire in `PageDesigner` (child key already pinned canonical `children` by #5027) but adds a designer behavior to maintain forever; B removes a permanent obligation but touches 4 type sites + 11 producers + the published guide row.
Recommendation: **B** (retire the key everywhere incl. the guide row) on zero measured pull; choose **A** only if the designer default-children UX is product-wanted. Options: A (wire `children: paletteItem?.defaultChildren ?? []`) / B (retire key + declarations + docs row).
Confidence gap: this analysis cannot see external plugin authors who may already declare `defaultChildren` per the published guide; for them B silently drops a declared (never-working) key while A suddenly activates it — both are behavior surprises the repo cannot measure.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5656 (`domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record). Landing gated on terminal success of every required job, read by name; see the bottom.

## The dispatch was wrong and checking it was the whole job

My brief said *"There is no maintainer ruling on this key that I know of, so treat retirement as needing one unless you find otherwise."* You found otherwise. **I verified it myself rather than taking your word**: comment two on this issue, `os-elon`, 2026-08-19, recording the maintainer's verbatim 「全部接受」 — **Option B, retire `defaultChildren` everywhere**, with the published guide row required in the same PR per ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, Option A rejected *for now*, and the state moved `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

So the fork was **not live**, no dev judgement was needed, and clause ② was already cleared by an authority.

**This is the fourth time in three rounds that a dispatch of mine contradicted the record — and the first time the mechanism is identifiable rather than just "from memory".** I read this card's body out of a cached `list_issues` payload. That payload carries `body` and **not** `comments`. My own standing rule — *read the whole comment thread before dispatching, every time* — was silently bypassed by the way I sourced the card, and the ruling was sitting **two comments above my own claim**.

Correctable, and now standing: **a cached list payload is not a card read.** Any card sourced that way gets its thread fetched before dispatch. The `unless you find otherwise` hedge is what kept this from becoming a false `needs_decision` escalation that would have spent the maintainer's attention re-answering a question they answered on 2026-08-19 — but a hedge is not a substitute for reading the thread.

## The consumer sweep is the gold standard for this lane

A zero is only evidence if the pipeline is proven able to hit. Yours doesn't just show a control returning non-zero — **the identical pipeline run against `defaultProps` returns 183 hits and *includes the known consumer*, `PageDesigner.tsx:173`.** That proves the pipeline finds the exact class of thing it is claiming is absent, which is a stronger control than "some other symbol resolves".

And you closed the hole a literal grep leaves open: no bracket access, no case-variant spelling, and the drop path **destructures `paletteItem` field-by-field with no wholesale spread** — so there is no dynamic read for a literal search to miss. That is the difference between "I grepped and found nothing" and "nothing can read it".

Counts re-measured 4 / 11 / 0 / 1, with only line numbers drifted (`types/base.ts` 508→540, `span.tsx` 138→160).

## Two void ablation legs, reported rather than buried

This is the part I want on the record:

- one leg logged to a path containing a `/` from the package name, so the **redirect** failed and the non-zero status was **bash's, not `tsc`'s**;
- another used a `perl` replacement containing `//`, which terminated the regex so the file never changed — caught by the **on-disk anchor check**, not by an exit code.

Both are in the PR body. Your own line for why: *"silently retrying until something lands is how the same defect gets copied up a level."* Exactly right — a void leg quietly re-run is indistinguishable from a leg that passed, which is the defect class this lane has spent the whole session on. Two more faces of measurement trap #4, in shapes not previously recorded here.

The real legs then measured **red** on both packages — `type-check EXIT=2`, `error TS2578: Unused @ts-expect-error directive` — which is a well-chosen pin: re-declaring the key makes the directive unused, so the assertion fails *by name* rather than by absence.

## Shipped bytes, with the type-only question settled first

The right order, and you did it: `.d.ts` removals erase at runtime, so the only runtime-bearing removal is the **zod mirror**. Measured — `dist/zod/base.zod.js` now `defaultChildren` **0** / `defaultProps` **1**, zero occurrences across `types/dist` and `core/dist`, **while the same grep still finds `defaultProps` in 8 dist files**. The control is inside the measurement rather than beside it.

Also correct: dropping the now-unused `SchemaNode` type import in `Registry.ts`, whose last user was the deleted line.

## You sharpened the ruling's own confidence gap

The ruling notes that external plugin authors' declared keys are silently dropped either way and calls the changeset the loud signal. You measured what "silently" actually means: **`ComponentMetaSchema` is a plain `z.object` with no `.strict()`, and zod 4.4.3 *strips* unknown keys** — so an external author who followed the published guide keeps a **valid** meta and loses the key with no diagnostic, while TypeScript authors get the loud signal. That is a concrete shape for a gap the ruling could only state in the abstract, and it belongs in the tombstone reasoning.

## Landing

Path surface is `packages/types/**`, `packages/core/**`, `packages/components/**` and `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` plus the changeset. **Root `skills/**` is not governed** — ordinary code PR, queue-eligible; `Skill Guide Path Check` is green.

**Correction to the shipped-bytes characterization** (does not change the ACCEPT — the change is correct and the effect is intended).

The report says *"the one runtime-bearing removal is the zod mirror"*, and the `dist` sweep was scoped to `types/dist` and `core/dist`. But the **11 producer sites** (`sidebar.tsx` ×10, `span.tsx`) are runtime object literals in register meta, so removing them is also runtime-bearing — in `packages/components`, which that sweep did not cover.

CI measured it independently. `Bundle Analysis` on this PR versus the same job on the sibling round-12 PR at the current baseline:

| | `components (index.js)` | gzipped |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (#5657, and every round-11 PR) | 507.00 KB | 113.72 KB |
| **#5656** | **506.21 KB** | **113.58 KB** |

So the retirement reaches shipped bytes in **two** places, not one, and the second is the larger of the two. That is a better result than the report claims — the producer literals really were being carried into the bundle for a key nothing read.

Recorded because the report's own discipline is the right one and this is the same shape it warns about: a `dist` sweep scoped to the packages you edited *declarations* in will miss the package you edited *producers* in. The sweep's scope, not its method, was the gap.
